ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the bottom of the figure is a common wire, which I label as the reference ground. The left branch is an upward current source, labeled 10u(t) A; the upper node is connected to the middle branch and the right branch. The middle branch from top to bottom is, in order, a controlled voltage source, with polarity positive at the top and negative at the bottom, voltage 2i_x, and then a 5Ω resistor connected to the bottom reference line. At the top of the right branch there is a 2 H inductor, the inductor current i_x is to the right, and after the inductor is connected a vertical 5Ω resistor, with the voltage across the resistor labeled v_0(t), positive at the top and negative at the bottom. Reasoning: When t → ∞, the circuit reaches DC steady state, and the 2 H inductor is equivalent to a short circuit. Therefore the top end of the right-side 5Ω resistor and the upper main node are the same node, and its voltage is v_0. Since i_x flows through the short circuit into the right-side 5Ω resistor, i_x = v_0/5, that is, v_0 = 5i_x. Let the downward current in the middle branch be i_m. Along the middle branch from the upper node to the reference ground, the voltage drop of the controlled voltage source is 2i_x, and the voltage drop of the lower 5Ω resistor is 5i_m, so v_0 = 2i_x + 5i_m. Write KCL for the upper node: the current source provides 10 A when t → ∞, which divides into the right branch and the middle branch, so 10 = i_x + i_m. Combining v_0 = 5i_x and v_0 = 2i_x + 5i_m gives 5i_x = 2i_x + 5i_m, therefore 3i_x = 5i_m, i_m = 0.6i_x. Substitute into 10 = i_x + i_m: 10 = 1.6i_x, obtaining i_x = 6.25 A. Thus v_0 = 5i_x = 31.25 V.
